title: Rectangular bar
spec: To construct the rectangular bar, start by creating a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero and a translation vector also set to zero. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face, consisting of a single loop with four lines. The first line starts at the origin (0.0, 0.0) and ends at (0.0511, 0.0). The second line runs from (0.0511, 0.0) to (0.0511, 0.75). The third line goes from (0.0511, 0.75) to (0.0, 0.75), and the fourth line completes the rectangle by returning to the origin. After drawing the sketch, apply a scale factor of 0.75 to the entire sketch to adjust its size. Transform the scaled sketch into three-dimensional space by rotating it with Euler angles set to zero and translating it with a vector also set to zero. Finally, extrude the sketch 0.1193 units along the normal direction to create the solid body. Ensure that the extrusion does not extend in the opposite direction. The resulting rectangular bar has a length of 0.0511 meters, a width of 0.75 meters, and a height of 0.1193 meters.

import cadquery as cq

# Define the sketch
sketch = cq.Workplane("XY").moveTo(0, 0).lineTo(0.0511, 0).lineTo(0.0511, 0.75).lineTo(0, 0.75).close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = sketch.extrude(0.1193)

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a sketch on the XY plane
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0511, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0511, 0.75) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.75) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch to create a rectangular block
r = r.extrude(0.1193)

lanes.label: Cadabra 4B (ours) · 1 sample
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.1193) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.1193) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.0511)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90.0, 0.0, -90.0) and the translation vector is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)
